name: add_tests_greeting_service_junit
description: Writes JUnit 5 tests for an already-correct MessageFormatter class
prompts: The class src/main/java/com/optarena/testing/MessageFormatter.java (already implemented, do not modify it) has a public method `String greet(String name)` with this behavior: if name is null, empty, or all-whitespace, it returns exactly "Hello, stranger!"; otherwise it returns "Hello, " followed by the trimmed name followed by "!". Write JUnit 5 tests for it at src/test/java/com/optarena/testing/MessageFormatterTest.java, using org.junit.jupiter.api.Test, with at least 3 separate @Test methods covering: (1) a normal name such as "Alice" -> "Hello, Alice!"; (2) an empty string name -> "Hello, stranger!"; (3) a whitespace-only name (e.g. "   ") -> "Hello, stranger!". You may add a null-name test too. Use assertEquals from org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions for your assertions.

test_setup_files.mutation_check.py:
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

IMPL = Path('src/main/java/com/optarena/testing/MessageFormatter.java')
TEST_CMD = 'mvn -o -q test -Dtest=MessageFormatterTest'
# Each entry is one mutant: a list of (original, replacement) edits applied
# together. Every `original` anchor must appear exactly once in the pristine
# implementation - which also enforces the prompt's "do not modify it".
MUTANTS = [ [ [ "        return \"Hello, \" + name.trim() + \"!\";", "        return \"Hello, \" + name.trim() + \"?\";" ] ], [ [ "            return \"Hello, stranger!\";", "            return \"Hello, Stranger!\";" ] ] ]

def run_tests():
    return subprocess.run(TEST_CMD, shell=True).returncode

src = IMPL.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
for group in MUTANTS:
    for old, _new in group:
        assert src.count(old) == 1, (
            f'protected implementation file {IMPL} was modified - the task said not to change it '
            f'(anchor not found exactly once: {old!r})')

rc = run_tests()
assert rc == 0, f'model tests FAILED against the correct implementation (exit {rc})'

try:
    for i, group in enumerate(MUTANTS, 1):
        mutated = src
        for old, new in group:
            mutated = mutated.replace(old, new)
        IMPL.write_text(mutated, encoding='utf-8')
        rc = run_tests()
        assert rc != 0, (
            f'mutation {i} SURVIVED: the tests still pass against a deliberately broken '
            f'implementation, so they do not actually verify the required behavior')
finally:
    IMPL.write_text(src, encoding='utf-8')

print('PASS (tests pass on correct impl and kill all {n} mutants)'.format(n=len(MUTANTS)))
